normalization: Header names are lowercase and their order is ignored; header values are preserved.
Optional whitespace after the Content-Type semicolon is ignored: Hono's fast and general response paths differ here.
JSON response bodies are compared structurally with object/array distinction; text bodies are compared byte-for-byte.
Middleware trace order and individual parameter values are preserved.

profile.expected: Ordered matches, per-handler before-next params, optional terminal params, segment regex, wildcard boundaries and strict slashes are covered by http.json and OrderedRouterTest.
PHP restores the caller's own params after next(); upstream keeps the last downstream route active. Both upstream output and explicit PHP target are retained in ordered-overlap.
strict=false normalizes only route matching; req.path retains the original encoded URI path, including the trailing slash. A dedicated PHP contract test covers this policy.
Onion order, short circuit, return after next, explicit replacement and handled errors are covered by http.json.
Percent decoding, duplicate queries, JSON and repeated body reads and urlencoded arrays are covered by http.json.
Malformed percent encoding/UTF-8 is HTTP 400; raw body buffering is bounded at 8388608 bytes by default. These PHP policies are checked in PHP unit tests, not generated by the JS harness.
Request-state isolation and response replacement are represented in http.json.
Context::extension() uses a class-string key and checks instanceof; PHP-only contract tests cover absent/null/wrong type and identity.
HEAD uses GET handlers but preserves the raw HEAD method, suppresses output bytes; method miss is 404.
Built-in PHP middleware APIs and SAPI limits have dedicated PHP tests. This core fixture corpus does not claim differential coverage of every middleware.

Only OPTIONS with Origin and Access-Control-Request-Method is a PHP preflight; ordinary OPTIONS continues. No Origin yields no Access-Control-Allow-Origin even for wildcard. Wildcard credentials are rejected, and the CORS policy is reapplied after downstream. CoreMiddlewareTest covers these PHP policies; http.json does not contain generated CORS cases.

PHP uses SHA-256 and never reads a HEAD body to create an ETag. Existing validators can produce 304; nonseekable and streaming bodies are skipped. AdvancedMiddlewareTest covers selected representation and compression order; no digest parity with upstream is claimed.
In-process request isolation is covered by http.json; SAPI/FPM/FrankenPHP have their own PHP integration tests, without a JS runtime equivalent.
Middle/suffix wildcards, multiple optional parameters, cross-segment regex, capturing groups, lookaround and backreferences are rejected. Raw multipart parsing is outside this profile.
